overview: The test suite is the largest single subsystem of the repo: 209 test files containing roughly 2,700 test functions under src/tests/. It is organized into unit/ (about 150 files covering ingest, features, models, CV splitters, dashboards, and the GSVIVS signal stack), integration/ (19 files that run multi-component workflows), formulas/ (a paper-audited registry where every mathematical function is checked against hand-computed gold values in JSON), graphs/ (graph construction for the GNN path), plus slow/, scripts/, and research/ folders. The design principle, stated in the integration conftest, is that no test needs the GS network: tick data normally comes from the internal Chunk Store via pytickclient, so tests replace it with mocked chunk_query responses and synthetic generators. The shared conftest simulates one trading day as 23,400 GBM ticks with a known 20 percent annualized vol, giving every estimator test an analytical ground truth; variants inject a 3 percent jump at tick 10,000 so jump-robust estimators (bipower variation, tripower quarticity, the BNS test) can be checked for both false positives and detection power. Daily-frequency fixtures build AR(1) log-RV series with HAR-like persistence. Integration tests then prove each model family end to end through the Pipeline class: HAR with the Duan retransformation correction, HARX with YAML-declared extra features, LightGBM with the QLIKE custom objective, TCN and LSTM (with context vectors) over mocked 5-minute sequence tensors, and a real GATv2 GNN over a correlation graph. Tournament-level tests cover single-model degenerate cases (DM stat 0, MCS trivially includes the model), checkpoint resume that skips already-run models, and a smoke test that the GSVIVS01 variance swap PnL section renders into the dashboard HTML. The restore has gaps: several modules the tests import, including volforecast/config.py and pipeline/runner.py, are absent from disk.

modules.role: Root of the suite; its conftest.py is the fixture factory the whole suite leans on. It simulates GBM log-price paths (23,400 ticks per day, true annualized vol 0.20), tick DataFrames shaped exactly like fetch_trades output with America/New_York timestamps, 500-day AR(1) log-RV series with HAR-like persistence, and 1000-row HAR feature matrices with aligned next-day targets. Autouse fixtures neutralize GS-only infrastructure: one fakes the pyslang session flag, another substitutes a MagicMock for the pytickclient processor so chunk-store logic is exercisable on any machine. Eight top-level test files cover LSTM and GNN model internals directly.

key_files.purpose: Shared synthetic data generators: GBM tick paths with known vol, jump-injected paths, AR(1) daily RV series, HAR feature matrices, and a tmp workspace layout.

modules.role: About 150 files of fast unit tests spanning the whole pipeline: data ingest (ticks, OHLCV, IV, GEX, credit CDS, VIX options), feature layers (asymmetry, microstructure, IV surface, dealer gamma, regime), every model family (HAR variants, LightGBM, XGBoost, LSTM, TCN, GNN, ensembles, blends), CV splitters with purge gaps, checkpointing, dashboards, and the GSVIVS signal and backtest stack. The heaviest files are test_models.py (80 tests), test_dashboard.py (72), and test_features.py (64). It feeds confidence into the integration layer, which reuses the same synthetic fixtures at larger scale.

key_files.purpose: 80 tests over the model registry and per-model fit/predict contracts.
48 tests on expanding-window and blocked k-fold CV including purge-gap leakage protection.

modules.role: A formula verification registry unique to this repo: FORMULAS.md maps every mathematical function to its source paper, exact equation number, implementation file, test file, and a gold_values JSON of hand-computed expected outputs. Fourteen test files marked pytest.mark.formula cover RV, RQ and tripower quarticity, BPV, semivariances, realized kernel, jump detection, QLIKE, the Diebold-Mariano test, VRP, VPIN, GFEVD spillovers, and the magnetic Laplacian. The conftest exposes a load_gold factory fixture that reads known-answer inputs from gold_values/. The registry also records known gaps, such as the unverified equation number for realized moments in Amaya et al. 2015.

key_files.purpose: Audit table linking each formula to paper, equation, implementation, test, and gold-value file.
Verifies QLIKE against Patton (2011) Eq. (5) including its minimum at truth and asymmetric penalty.

modules.role: Nineteen files that run multi-component workflows on synthetic data with no network or real files, per the conftest docstring. test_data_pipeline.py (57 tests) proves the mocked Chunk Store path: symbol universe, E-mini quarterly contract rolling, batch fetching with per-day API calls, tick resampling to 5-minute bars, and the daily RV measure dictionary. test_rv_pipeline.py (60 tests) validates estimators against GBM ground truth and runs the full simulate-prices to HAR to QLIKE loop, including the Duan retransformation correction. Model-specific pipeline tests (LightGBM, TCN, LSTM context, GNN, HARX) each prove one model family survives the real Pipeline CV loop end to end, and tournament tests cover checkpoint resume, single-model degenerate statistics, and dashboard output.

key_files.purpose: Integration fixtures: 500-day HAR-like RV series and a 3-symbol by 320-day AR(1) panel for graph tests.
Chunk Store mocking, ES contract rolls, tick resampling, and the daily RV measure dict.
Estimator correctness on GBM paths plus the full RV-to-HAR-to-metrics loop and Duan correction.
Proves resumed tournaments skip checkpointed models and reproduce identical predictions.

modules.role: Tests that read real data from data/processed/ or data/raw/ and are excluded from the default pytest run via pyproject.toml; run explicitly with uv run pytest tests/slow/. Currently holds a single GPU scaling test. Several integration tests (TCN, LSTM context, GNN) also carry the slow marker so the fast ./vol test loop skips torch training.

These pin tournament outputs against regression rather than recomputing them from scratch.

glossary.definition: The quasi-likelihood loss from Patton (2011), QLIKE(sigma2, h) = log(h) + sigma2/h, the primary evaluation metric of the project. It is minimized when the forecast equals the true variance, is robust to noisy volatility proxies, and penalizes under-prediction more than over-prediction.
The sum of squared intraday returns over a trading day, here computed from 5-minute bars. It is the target quantity the whole project forecasts.
A jump-robust variance estimator built from products of adjacent absolute returns. Without jumps it approximates RV; with a jump it stays below RV, and that gap is the basis for jump detection.
The Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard z test comparing RV to BPV, scaled by tripower quarticity (TPQ), which is used instead of standard realized quarticity because RQ is inflated by the jump itself.
A microstructure-noise-robust volatility estimator; the tests require it to beat naive tick-level RV at recovering the true variance from noisy prices.
The split of RV into upside (positive-return) and downside (negative-return) halves; the two components must sum exactly back to RV.

The heterogeneous autoregressive model of realized volatility, regressing next-day log RV on daily, weekly, and monthly RV averages; the project's baseline model and the dynamic its synthetic fixtures imitate.

A retransformation (smearing) correction applied when converting log-space predictions back to variance space; for Gaussian OLS residuals it approximates half the residual variance, and for QLIKE-trained models it is near zero.
The model confidence set, the collection of models not statistically distinguishable from the best; with only one entrant it trivially includes that model with p-value 1.
The classic test of equal predictive accuracy between two forecast series, per Diebold and Mariano (1995); implemented in evaluation/statistical_tests.py and verified against gold values.
A GS variance swap index whose PnL section the tournament dashboard renders; tests substitute a synthetic random-walk level series so no TSDB access is required.

A buffer of trading days excluded between the training and test windows in cross validation so overlapping multi-day RV targets cannot leak future information into training; integration configs use purge_gap=5.
